Its agentic capabilities enable it to work across applications, use contextual information, adapt to obstacles, and request clarification or approval when necessary. results.title: Muse Wonder: A Frontier Model For Personal & Professional AI Agents
results.content:
### Frontier Coding

Coding brings these capabilities together. Building software requires tracking requirements, making changes across a codebase, and working through repeated cycles of testing and revision. Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full deliver frontier coding performance, supporting projects from small applications to complex software. We trained both models on diverse, long-running tasks to help them sustain progress across this process.

## Capabilities That Generalize

Two models often have similar benchmark scores, yet one seems to handle a much wider range of unfamiliar tasks. That’s what complaints of “benchmaxxing” and praise for “big model smell” both get at: a breadth of capability that popular benchmarks in a few domains can’t fully capture.

results.title: Theo Browne: Meta's Muse Wonder Full Is the First Non-OpenAI, Non-Anthropic Model Worth Daily-Driving — BigGo Finance
results.content:
| Model | Availability | Speed | Published price | Browne's assessment |
 ---  --- 
| Muse Wonder | API + subscription | ~120 TPS | $4/M in, $20/M out, $0.20 cache reads | Bad model for the price; not compelling |
| Muse Wonder Full | Muse Code subscription only | ~50 TPS | Not published | Neck-and-neck with Astra and Fable on real-world work; pleasant to use |

The API-available standard Muse Wonder is a separate problem. On Browne's T3 Code architecture audit, it scored less than half of Opus's score — a drop of over 30% versus Muse Wonder Full. On another audit it scored 5.75 out of 10 versus Soul's 9. "I suspect many negative online demos are using the API-available standard model and concluding the release is bad," Browne noted. He's probably right. [...] There's also a hint of something Gemini-like baked in. Browne ran Skatebench, a benchmark he'd stopped using because it produces odd results — Opus 5 Max scored 84% and 5.5 Max 79%, suggesting RL nerfs models on it. Only Gemini models had ever broken 90%. Muse Wonder Full scored 95%. That initially worried him, because Gemini models share a cluster of traits he finds concerning. His testing found the skateboard-trick ability didn't nerf the model elsewhere. It's "some of that same weirdness baked in" rather than a sign of general superiority.

### The weak points are real [...] ### The weak points are real

Browne is blunt about the model's limitations. UI work is atrocious — not wrong the way Grok's is, but slop the way Sonnet 3.7's was. 3D is poor. A tractor demo comparing Opus 5.5 to Muse Wonder Full shows a clear gap, and the Blender output is "absolute garbage" with bad coloring and lighting. Meta itself lists visual and spatial reasoning, especially 3D tasks, as a known limitation.
